From: Josh Reed <josh.reed@solvent.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production latency spike impacting inference responses

Markus —

We observed a sustained latency spike across our inference calls to model redwood/gpt-4s-hr at about 08:45 PST. P99 jumped from ~220ms to >2.4s and a few requests timed out at 30s. This affected our user flows for ~35 minutes and triggered multiple downstream retries.

Can you confirm if this was on your side and share a brief timeline and immediate mitigation steps? We need an internal note for our incident review and a statement for execs.

Thanks,
Josh Reed
Director, Site Reliability — Solvent.io

[Attachment: request-logs-ops-0628.zip (log bundle stub)]

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Josh Reed <josh.reed@solvent.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-28T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Production latency spike impacting inference responses

Josh —

First, I’m very sorry for the disruption and the downstream impact on your product. Thank you for flagging this so quickly and for the log bundle — that helped. High level summary up front:

- What happened: a transient KV-cache eviction storm combined with a model worker retry cascade during an autoscaler cooldown window.
- Impact window: 08:43–09:18 PST (35 minutes).
- User-visible symptoms: elevated p95/p99 latency and occasional 30s timeouts for affected routes.
- Immediate mitigation: we temporarily increased worker pool headroom, disabled aggressive autoscale cooldowns, and rolled a hotfix to KV eviction throttling at 09:05 PST.

Attached is our short RCA summary (solvent-20270629-rca-summary.pdf) and a CSV with the eviction/timeline snippet you can ingest (kv-eviction-timeline.csv). We’ll follow up with the full technical appendix and post-incident changelog.

Action items we own (short-term):
1) Firewall aggressive eviction path by implementing a tokenized backoff (complete 2027-06-29 12:00 PST).
2) Add a health-check-driven autoscaler override to prevent scale-in during elevated latency (ETA 2 weeks).
3) Share a replayable test harness for your team to run against a staging variant (ETA 1 week).

What we request from Solvent: a snippet of representative production traffic (anonymized) to validate the harness and a 30-minute follow-up call so we can run through mitigations and timelines with your SREs.

Again — apologies. We’ll keep this thread as the canonical customer-facing record.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: solvent-20270629-rca-summary.pdf; kv-eviction-timeline.csv]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-28T13:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Production latency spike impacting inference responses

Markus —

Quick technical addendum for the thread (for Solvent we can keep this condensed):

- Root cause details: a GC pattern in one of the memory-constrained worker instance classes caused a temporary spike in memory pressure; that triggered KV-cache eviction across a small fraction of shards. Evictions caused cache-miss amplification because clients retried aggressively; retries hit the already-stressed worker set and produced the observed tail-latency.
- Why autoscaler didn’t help: the cluster scaled out after the spike began but a cooldown policy prevented immediate additional capacity; by the time new workers were fully ready, retry traffic had already amplified.
- Short-term mitigation implemented: eviction rate limiter + transient retry-window suppression (hotfix rolled at 09:05 PST).
- Longer-term: waveform-based autoscaler signals and a small margin buffer for the affected instance class.

I’ve pasted a short timeline snapshot below for inclusion in the customer appendix.

[Timeline snapshot]
08:41 PST — background batch job increases memory usage on 7% of workers
08:43 PST — eviction events begin to spike (clients see elevated latency)
08:46 PST — retries amplify traffic; p99 > 2s
09:05 PST — hotfix: eviction throttling & retry suppression rolled; headroom increased
09:18 PST — metrics return to baseline

I can prepare a one-page engineering appendix if you want me to join the follow-up call.

— Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Josh —

Following our internal verification and the joint review with Solvent SREs this morning, we’re closing this incident record with the actions below and a link to the consolidated appendix. Thank you for the collaboration and for the logs you provided — they were critical for reproducing the sequence.

What we completed:
- Immediate mitigations: eviction throttling + retry suppression (hotfix) verified on 2027-06-28 09:05 PST.
- Post-incident fixes shipped to staging: autoscaler cooldown override and a margin buffer configuration (deployed to staging 2027-06-29 11:20 PST).
- Observability: added an eviction-rate alert and a P99 headroom dashboard (live 2027-06-29 14:00 PST).
- Customer playground: shared test harness and ingest instructions (Drive link below).

Open items and timeline:
- Production autoscaler policy change (rollout): 2 weeks (tentative completion 2027-07-13).
- Full engineering appendix and replayable artifact: 2027-07-06.
- Post-deployment verification window with Solvent (30m): please let us know availability the week of 2027-07-05.
